narrative.overview:
Plastiverse Live is told as one passage from darkness into light. The story opens on a pure black ground where real photographed plastics and real paper pages sit under hard light; once the knowledge bulb bursts, the page turns to an airy, nearly white ground and everything after is flat data drawn in navy ink and slate, with a single coral mark for what is live. The light half is the working half of the system: calm, square, hairline-ruled, generous with air, and quiet enough that the one coral mark carries the meaning.

The system is restrained by default and dramatic only once, in the landing story. Type is a regular-weight grotesk set large with tight tracking, so headlines read as plain statements rather than shouts; a narrow monospace appears only where a number or a source is being cited. There are no rounded corners, no decorative shadows, and no ornament on the light ground beyond a faint 24 px grid behind the regions band.
keyCharacteristics: Two grounds: black for the story and the footer, a cool near-white for everything else.
Navy ink, slate data, coral only for "live".
Regular-weight headlines with -0.03em tracking; monospace only for data and sources.
Square corners and 1 px hairlines; no rounded surfaces, no card shadows.
Real photographs and paper pages before the light; flat data marks after it.

rules.name: The Coral Ink Rule
rules.body: On a light ground coral is a fill or large text only; any coral text, arrow or focus ring at body size uses coral-ink. On the black ground, coral itself is used.

rules.name: The One Live Mark Rule
rules.body: In every data graphic, coral marks the single live or featured thing (California, the live atlas row, the last mark of each pictogram); everything else is ink, slate or mint. If two things on one view are coral, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Mint After Dark Rule
rules.body: Mint is text only on the black ground. On light it may appear only as a data-ramp fill step, never as text.

rules.name: The Mono Is Evidence Rule
rules.body: Martian Mono sets numbers, axis and table labels, legends and source lines, and nothing else: never a heading, button, link or label above a heading.

rules.name: The Regular-Weight Headline Rule
rules.body: Headlines are weight 400 with negative tracking; size, not weight, makes hierarchy. Weight 700 belongs to the wordmark alone.

rules.name: The Measured Safe Zone Rule (landing-only)
rules.body: Story text never overlaps an image. Layout measures each caption's text box and places every visual right of the widest side caption plus 40 px (or 40% of the width, whichever is greater) on desktop, and between the top and bottom captions at 860 px or less.

rules.name: The Flat Light Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the light ground casts a shadow. A surface that needs separating gets a hairline or a paper fill.

rules.name: The Live Atlas Rule
rules.body: In the app, coral fills and coral tints (7% at rest, 12 to 14% on hover) belong to the live regional atlas (California) and its entry points alone: its map cells and callout, its ladder step, its table sub-row, its overview box and its drawer row. An atlas in preparation gets a dashed coral-ink swatch or outline, never a fill; a requestable region gets a plain ink-2 outline. Ordinary hover and selection tints are slate (6% hover, 8% list hover, 10% current row), never coral.

rules.name: The Source Line Rule
rules.body: Every data view in the app ends in an 11 px mono source line in ink-2 (line height 1.6, max 100ch, 12 px above). Illustrative counts and preview limits are stated there in plain words ("Illustrative counts, scaled to ...", "This preview hides titles that ..."), never left implicit.

dos: Do use the `--pv-*` tokens for every colour in CSS; canvas code mirrors them as constants.
Do use coral-ink for any coral text, arrow or focus ring on a light ground.
Do give every interactive element the 2 px coral-ink focus ring with a 3 px offset.
Do set headlines at weight 400 with -0.03em tracking and balanced wrapping.
Do keep corners square and separate surfaces with 1 px ink or line rules.
Do draw icons as inline SVG using `currentColor` or the token fills.
Do label illustrative data as illustrative, in an 11 px mono source line under it.
Do keep story text out of image boxes by measuring caption boxes, and test it.
Do keep coral fills and tints for the live regional atlas; use slate tints for ordinary hover and selection.
Do announce every scope change in one polite live region and carry scope and view in the URL.
Do end every data view with an 11 px mono source line that names illustrative data and preview limits.
Do show an honest notice with links to profiles that exist when a view has no data, rather than an empty chart.
Do zoom the map to a new scope over 450 ms ease-out, and jump instantly under reduced motion.
donts: Don't put an eyebrow or kicker label above a heading.
Don't use Martian Mono for headings, buttons or navigation.
Don't set mint text on a light ground.
